title: Beef Bourguignon
subtitle: Classic French braised beef in Burgundy red wine
excerpt: Chunks of braising beef slow-cooked in red wine with lardons, mushrooms, and pearl onions until tender and glossy. One of the great French braises.

recipe.sourceNotes: Boeuf bourguignon is one of the great dishes of French cuisine, originating in Burgundy, where both the beef and the wine it is cooked in come from. It was traditionally a peasant dish made by slowly braising tough, cheap cuts of beef in wine to tenderise them, but was elevated to haute cuisine by Julia Child, whose 1961 recipe in Mastering the Art of French Cooking brought the dish to American and subsequently British home cooks. The method of browning the beef, vegetables, and lardons separately before braising, and reducing the wine in which the beef has marinated, builds layers of flavour that cannot be shortcut. The dish is always better the next day after the flavours have had time to develop overnight in the refrigerator.

recipeTools.notes: A large casserole or Dutch oven with a lid.

content.text: Marinate the beef overnight in the wine if time allows: this deepens the flavour. Dry the beef thoroughly before browning or it will steam rather than colour. Brown in batches over high heat. The dish can be cooked the day before and gently reheated: the flavour improves overnight. Skim the fat from the surface before serving.

items.preparation: full-bodied; Burgundy, Merlot, or Côtes du Rhône
small, peeled whole; or use small pickling onions

content.text: Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Dry the beef thoroughly. Season with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a large casserole over high heat. Brown the beef in batches until deeply coloured. Remove and set aside. Brown the lardons until crisp. Remove.

Reduce heat. Add the shallots and cook for 5 minutes until beginning to colour. Add the garlic and tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Sprinkle over the flour and stir for 1 minute. Return the beef and lardons. Pour in the wine and stock. Add the thyme and bay leaves.

Bring to a simmer. Cover and transfer to the oven for 2 hours until the beef is very tender. Fry the mushrooms in butter until golden. Add to the casserole for the last 30 minutes. Remove thyme and bay. Skim any fat from the surface. Taste for seasoning. Scatter with parsley. Serve with mashed potato, noodles, or crusty bread.
